prompt:
I need the front end for Jotsy. A free shared-notes app with tens of millions of casual users, where friends, roommates and families write and keep checklists and plans together.

Who's using it: Kenji Morales, 26, one of five roommates moving out of the rented house they've shared for three years. He's the organized one, but is far from a project manager.

What they're doing right now: The lease ends November 30. Kenji started a shared note called 'Move-Out: 412 Alder St' to split up the cleaning, sort out who keeps which shared furniture and track what's needed to get the deposit back. Right now three roommates have it open at once. Lucía is claiming the couch at the same moment Priya is adding the couch to the 'sell' section. Someone deleted the oven-cleaning task yesterday and nobody admits it. Kenji wants to see who changed what, restore the deleted task and assign the remaining tasks. He also wants to give the landlord view-and-comment access to the inspection section only, so she can't edit the roommates' private notes about splitting money.

What's in the system at this point: Note 'Move-Out: 412 Alder St', created Nov 2, 2026, with sections: Cleaning Tasks (23 items, 9 done, each with an assignee and a due date), Shared Furniture (11 items: couch, dining table, 2 bookshelves, TV, etc., each marked keep, sell, donate or undecided, plus who claimed it), Deposit Checklist (14 items from the lease's inspection list; deposit 3,250), Utilities and Forwarding (6 items) and Money Notes (private to roommates). Collaborators: Kenji (owner), Lucía, Priya, Sam, Theo (editors), landlord Marjorie Chen (invited, not yet accepted). Edit history: 187 changes over two weeks, with the oven-cleaning task deleted Nov 15 at 22:41 by Theo's phone. Currently present: Kenji, Lucía, Priya. Comments: 8 open, including Sam's 'who's renting the van?'

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
